a residential San Antonio neighborhood, muddy stormwater floods a front yard and reaches boot height before a cell phone on the porch railing
finally receives an emergency flash flood alert. To address this dangerous latency, UT San Antonio researchers designed a self-powered flood station
prototype that harvests ambient light and operates independently of cellular towers. The station mounts four optical sensors at varying heights along its post to track
rising water while auxiliary sensors monitor rain, temperature, humidity, and light. An integrated TinyML chip processes these environmental readings locally, determining
flood risk without contacting an external server. The station transmits its alert via long-range radio up to a half-mile
through city streets or five miles across open terrain to a central monitoring hub. There, a secondary AI model aggregates station data to project
predictive flood inundation maps for emergency responders. The report concludes by noting that while lab validation reached 98.82

% accuracy, no field installations have yet taken place, leaving deployment as an ongoing goal.",
